extra.message: User input from POST /students/ (data['name']) flows into Student.create() which uses Python string formatting (% operator) to interpolate the name directly into the SQL query: "VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name}. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL, e.g., submitting name='); DROP TABLE students; --.

Jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False, disabling automatic HTML escaping for all template output. This is the root cause of multiple Stored XSS vulnerabilities throughout the application, as user-controlled data (student names, course titles/descriptions, review text) is rendered without escaping.

User-controlled student name is rendered without escaping via {{ name }}. Since autoescape is disabled, an attacker can inject <script> tags via the student name input (POST /students/), resulting in Stored XSS that executes for any user viewing the students list.

User-controlled course title is rendered without escaping via {{ course.title }}. An attacker can inject JavaScript via the course title input (POST /courses/), resulting in Stored XSS that executes for any user viewing the courses list.
User-controlled course description is rendered without escaping via {{ course.description }}. An attacker can inject JavaScript via the description input (POST /courses/), resulting in Stored XSS.
User-controlled course title is rendered without escaping via {{ course.title }} on the course detail page, allowing Stored XSS.
User-controlled course description is rendered without escaping via {{ course.description }} on the course detail page, allowing Stored XSS.

User-controlled review text is rendered without escaping via {{ review.review_text }}. An attacker can inject JavaScript via the review input (POST /courses/{id}/review), resulting in Stored XSS that executes for any user viewing the course page.
User-controlled course title is rendered without escaping in the breadcrumb navigation via {{ course.title }}, allowing Stored XSS.
User-controlled course title is rendered without escaping on the student marks page via {{ course.title }}, allowing Stored XSS.
User-controlled course description is rendered without escaping on the student marks page via {{ course.description }}, allowing Stored XSS.
User-controlled course title is rendered without escaping on the review page via {{ course.title }}, allowing Stored XSS.
User-controlled student name is rendered without escaping on the evaluate error page via {{ student.name }}, allowing Stored XSS.

The 50x error page renders {{ error.__dict__ }} which dumps the entire exception object's internal attributes. This can expose sensitive information such as database connection strings, configuration values, file paths, and stack traces to end users.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The CSRF middleware is commented out (# csrf_middleware), disabling CSRF protection for all state-changing operations. Templates include CSRF tokens but they are never verified. An attacker can craft malicious pages that submit forms to create students, courses, reviews, grades, or logout users without their consent.

Password verification uses unsalted MD5 hashing: md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest(). MD5 is cryptographically broken and too fast for password hashing. No salt is used, making the hashes vulnerable to rainbow table and brute-force attacks. If the database is compromised (e.g., via the SQL injection vulnerability), all passwords can be trivially cracked.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-759: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt

extra.message: The aiohttp Application is created with debug=True, which enables detailed error traces and debug information that could be exposed to end users, revealing internal application details.

The Redis session storage is configured with httponly=False, making the session cookie accessible to JavaScript. If an XSS vulnerability is exploited (multiple exist in this application), an attacker can steal the session cookie and hijack user sessions.

Database credentials (user: postgres, password: postgres) are hardcoded in the default configuration file config/dev.yaml, which is checked into the repository and used as the default config (app.py line 18: default_config='./config/dev.yaml').

The POST handler for /students/ has no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can create new student records. The @authorize() decorator is only applied to the logout endpoint but not to this state-changing operation.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The POST handler for /courses/ has no authentication or authorization check. Any unauthenticated user can create new course records. The template conditionally shows the form only to admin users, but the server-side handler does not enforce this restriction.

extra.message: The POST handler for /courses/{course_id}/review has no authentication check. Any unauthenticated user can submit reviews for any course.
